uncited: A regularization term that enforces semantic alignment between rendered images and text prompts by minimizing the distance between their embeddings in the CLIP latent space.

It differs from photometric losses by optimizing for high-level semantic consistency rather than pixel-wise intensity matching, enabling text-guided editing and semantic constraints in radiance fields.
Encode the rendered image $I$ into an embedding vector $v_{img} = E_{img}(I)$.
Encode the text prompt $T$ into an embedding vector $v_{txt} = E_{txt}(T)$.
Compute the cosine similarity between $v_{img}$ and $v_{txt}$.
Compute the loss as one minus the similarity.
- **Time complexity:** Dominated by the forward pass of the CLIP encoders, which is constant with respect to scene size but depends on image resolution and text length.
It is a foundational technique in semantic NeRF editing and inverse rendering.
